clue.text: Remove from fighting of French unruly crowd

parts.note: de is the French word for of
a mob is a disorderly crowd

explanation.surface: A French rabble pulled out of the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To demobilise troops is to release them from military service; the short form is the verb used here.

clue.text: City idol's strange meek quality

indicators.note: strange suggests these letters are to be made odd, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A town's hero is oddly mild-mannered.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link word, and its S is not part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Docility is a readiness to be led or taught, a gentle submissive trait.

clue.text: A large number drinking gallons, sick as a dog?

indicators.note: drinking means one piece swallows another, so it goes inside

parts.note: many means a large number

explanation.surface: Lots of people downing gallons and ending up ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: mange is a skin disease of dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog with mange has a scabby, hair-losing skin disease, so it is unwell in a canine way.

clue.text: Secondary highway to secure psychiatric hospital

parts.note: in Britain a B road is a secondary road, below an A road
to moor a boat is to secure it

explanation.surface: A minor road leading to a secure mental institution.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are graded A (major) and B (secondary). Broadmoor is a high-security psychiatric hospital in Berkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadmoor is a well-known secure mental hospital in England, an example of the kind.

clue.text: Fibres woven into underwear

indicators.note: woven says the threads of these letters are interlaced into a new pattern

explanation.surface: Fibres knitted together to make a pair of pants.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefs are short close-fitting pants, a kind of undergarment.

clue.text: Polish gemstone lacking finish

indicators.note: lacking its finish means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a ruby is a red gemstone

explanation.surface: Buffing up a jewel that hasn't had its final treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' at the start disguises the capital: it is the verb, not the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub a surface is to buff or shine it, as when polishing.

clue.text: Speedo I rigged is only part of the story

indicators.note: rigged means fixed or tampered with, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A swimmer admits that a tampered swimsuit is only half the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Speedo is a brand of swimwear.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is one instalment or incident within a longer narrative.

clue.text: Fine thread of singular type

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
ilk means kind or type

explanation.surface: A delicate strand of a unique sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Silk is the fine filament spun by silkworms, used for luxurious fabric.

clue.text: Sad, seeing the Spanish repeatedly beat Germany up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
to batter is to strike again and again

explanation.surface: A football report: a pity that Spain keep thrashing Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ELBATTERGER as it is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something regrettable is unfortunate and to be lamented, which makes it a sorry matter.

clue.text: Forgive swindle perpetrated

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
something perpetrated has been done

explanation.surface: Pardoning a fraud that someone has committed.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone a wrong is to overlook or excuse it, close to pardoning it.

clue.text: Fantastic fish

definitions.meaning: British slang, short for brilliant, meaning excellent
a European flatfish related to the turbot

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic cry about a wonderful catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the slang clipping of brilliant, and a flatfish caught off European coasts.

clue.text: Set down narrative poem for singing

definitions.meaning: to place something down is to put it flat
a ballad-like poem meant to be sung

explanation.surface: Writing out a ballad to be sung.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the verb meaning place, and a medieval term for a short sung story poem.

clue.text: Scornful behaviour, inside or out

indicators.note: out here means wrong or off, so these letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Mockery that can come from within a group or from outside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside or out' reads as a phrase, but 'out' is the anagram signal working on INSIDEOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Derision is contemptuous ridicule, which is scornful conduct towards someone.

clue.text: Foolishly accept lies without first bit of evidence? Unlikely to do that!

indicators.note: foolishly suggests these letters are jumbled up in a silly way
without means a letter is left out of the word
the first bit of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Swallowing falsehoods without proof is not something a doubter would do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes E (first bit of 'evidence') from LIES, leaving LIS; 'Foolishly' then shuffles ACCEPT and LIS. The definition points back at the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubter demands proof, so would not swallow untruths without any supporting facts.

clue.text: Struggle in which participants keep discounting earlier deals?

definitions.text: Struggle in which participants keep discounting earlier deals?

parts.words: Struggle in which participants keep discounting earlier deals?
parts.note: a battle between shops, each cutting below what rivals offered before

explanation.surface: Rival sides who ignore past agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discounting' suggests disregarding treaties, but means cutting prices below earlier offers.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight among retailers in which each repeatedly undercuts competitors' prices.

clue.text: Possible Oscar-winning performance when January begins?

definitions.meaning: a stage or screen act good enough to be judged best of the twelve months
the point where one calendar period ends and the next starts

explanation.surface: An acting triumph of New Year's Day timing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is cryptic: a 'turn' is a performance, so the best one of the year might win an Oscar.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a standout performance among a twelvemonth's acts, and the changeover between December and the new calendar.

clue.text: Managed most of trial venue in spite

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a court is where trials are held

explanation.surface: Running most of a courtroom out of malice.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep-seated bitterness or ill will, much like spite.

clue.text: Part of bound ream that is not thought of

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bundle of paper that nobody has considered.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'is not thought of' must be read with 'that' as 'that which is not thought of': something never imagined.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never imagined, not even in a fantasy, has not been conceived by anyone.

clue.text: This physician returned cash on delivery

indicators.note: returned tells the solver to send those letters back the other way

explanation.surface: A doctor who sent back a payment made on receipt.
explanation.definitionFit: Doc is an informal shortened form of doctor, a medical practitioner.

clue.text: Detective Inspector and Judge working where mustard comes from

parts.note: DI is the police abbreviation for Detective Inspector
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Police and judiciary at work in a condiment factory.
explanation.definitionFit: The French city in Burgundy gives its name to a famous pale, sharp mustard.

clue.text: Like a gift for the listener, spellbound

indicators.note: for the listener signals that the word is to be judged by how it is said

parts.note: a present is usually wrapped

explanation.surface: A child entranced, hearing a present unwrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enthralled is to be completely absorbed, as if under a spell.

clue.text: Try not to meet a very old identity

parts.note: ID is the short form of identity, as on an ID card

explanation.surface: Steering clear of a long-lost acquaintance.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun someone is to keep away from them deliberately, trying not to cross paths.

clue.text: Give colour to odd bits of Dryden

indicators.note: the odd bits are the first, third and fifth letters of the poet's name

explanation.surface: Adding colour to a few odd passages of the poet John Dryden.
explanation.definitionFit: To dye is to tint or stain something with a colouring agent.

clue.text: For Spooner, maybe Scottish legislation might be a cause of speech impediment

indicators.note: Spooner's name signals that the opening sounds of two words are to be swapped

parts.note: Jock is a familiar term for a Scotsman, used here as a modifier
law is legislation

explanation.surface: Scots law as a reason someone cannot talk properly.
explanation.walkthrough: JOCK LAW with its initial J and L exchanged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus clamps the jaw shut, which leaves the sufferer unable to speak clearly.

clue.text: Land fowl

definitions.meaning: a country, the nation straddling Europe and Asia
a large domesticated bird eaten at Christmas

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the country with Ankara as capital, and the big farmyard bird.

clue.text: Cores of blue and black materials from the moon

indicators.note: the core of each word is its central letter or letters, taken from all four words

explanation.surface: Samples of dark and blue stuff brought back from space.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunar describes anything relating to or coming from Earth's natural satellite.
